scenes.title: Names, places, and record
scenes.copy: A memorial-wall tone for western Pennsylvania — Context for the region, Evidence for what you can stand beside on the map.
scenes.narration: Welcome. I am David, your regional historian for western Pennsylvania and eastern Ohio. Tonight we walk The Valley as a HyperFrame gallery — scholastic wall text, not a brochure. Context means background. Evidence means places and published record. We begin at Buhl Park.

scenes.title: Satellite from the hub
scenes.copy: Every pin radiates from Hermitage’s free green. Ohio sites sit just across the state line.
scenes.narration: Open the atlas on satellite view. Buhl Park is the hub — Frank H. Buhl’s gift so working families could gather without a ticket. Select a pin for on-the-ground notes. The Youngstown corridor appears because the border is minutes away.

scenes.title: Fortune that funded a park
scenes.copy: Sharon Iron to Farrell’s mill — wealth, labor, and the endowment that still keeps golf free.
scenes.narration: Steel built this valley. Frank Buhl’s fortune rose with the mills; his philanthropy returned as Buhl Farm Park. Flip the first steel card — wall text, not romance. The Magic City of Farrell and the long mill closures are part of the same gallery.

scenes.title: New Wilmington, not Lancaster
scenes.copy: Old Order roads since eighteen forty-seven — courtesy first; people are not exhibits.
scenes.narration: Ten miles from the hub lies New Wilmington and Volant Amish country. This is a living settlement, not Lancaster tourism. Drive slowly for buggies. Photograph fields, not faces. Museum etiquette applies on the road as well as in the gallery.

scenes.title: Lettermen and Mercer County
scenes.copy: Tony Butala from Sharon; Trent Reznor from Mercer borough — same county, careful geography.
scenes.narration: Music leaves inscriptions too. Tony Butala of The Lettermen is Sharon’s harmony story. Trent Reznor grew up in Mercer — the county seat, not the mill towns. Keep the towns straight, the way a wall keeps dates straight.

scenes.title: Youngstown’s decisive decade
scenes.copy: Cleveland vs Pittsburgh for the bug and the tables — 1970s war while steel fell. Context vs Evidence on the wall.
scenes.narration: Now the Youngstown corridor — and the big chapter is the nineteen-seventies. No resident Mafia family; Cleveland and Pittsburgh fought for the Mahoning Valley. The Saturday Evening Post had already named Crime Town U.S.A. Then came the late-decade faction war, the Cleveland bombing that pulled in the Carabbias, and Charlie Carabbia’s nineteen-eighty disappearance — later sworn in court. Same decade, the mills died. Read the cards as a museum room. No romance. No rumor.

scenes.title: 1977 — mills and rackets, same decade
scenes.copy: Youngstown Sheet & Tube’s Campbell Works fell on 19 September 1977. Watch the archival mini-doc beside the mob gallery.
scenes.narration: Same decade as the faction war: Black Monday — September nineteenth, nineteen seventy-seven — when Youngstown Sheet and Tube closed Campbell Works and thousands lost work overnight. Scroll to Watch for the period mini-documentary. Steel collapse and contested rackets share one map.

scenes.title: Continue with the expert
scenes.copy: Eight gallery chapters await. Ask David about West Pennsylvania, East Ohio, or any pin on the satellite atlas.
scenes.narration: The reel stops here — once through, like a memorial highlight pass. Eight chapters on the wall. Ask me anything about western Pennsylvania or eastern Ohio. Facts first. Context labeled. Evidence preferred.
